summary: A proposal by Jon Postel for a standard Character Generator process that sends character data regardless of input, the opposite of the Discard process in RFC 348. Hosts that choose to could run it, using the Initial Connection Protocol, to help test terminals and connections.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 429 proposes a Character Generator process for hosts that want to provide one. After a connection is established, it sends characters until the connection closes.

questions: what is the character generator process
how does the proposed character generator work
subtitle: A proposed process that sends characters for network testing

tldr.problem: Hosts could benefit from a common process that supplies character data for testing, rather than relying on separate local programs.
tldr.mechanism: A host would accept a connection, complete the Initial Connection Protocol and send characters as buffer space became available.
tldr.outcome: The proposal defines a simple service that continues until the connection is closed.

today: RFC 429 proposes a Character Generator process and describes its connection behavior. It does not specify a socket number or require hosts to implement it.

sections.title: A Standard Character Generator
sections.content:
Jonathan Postel proposes a process that generates character data without regard to input. Hosts could choose whether to implement it. The RFC notes that existing terminal-testing programs on many hosts could serve this purpose.

The proposal describes the process as the converse of the Discard process.
sections.plainLanguage: A host could offer a process that sends characters without using the data it receives. The RFC presents this as a proposed standard service.

sections.title: Establishing and Closing a Connection
sections.content: The Character Generator would listen for a connection request and perform the Initial Connection Protocol described in the Current Network Protocols notebook. After that protocol completed, it would send characters as buffer space became available. Closing the connections would terminate the process.
sections.plainLanguage: The service first follows the network's connection procedure. It then sends characters when space is available and stops when the connections close.

sections.title: Host Implementation
sections.content: The RFC proposes that hosts implement the process if they choose to provide it. It does not specify a socket number, character sequence, data rate or required deployment.
sections.plainLanguage: Each host could decide whether to run the proposed service. The RFC leaves its exact socket number and character sequence unspecified.
